narrative: OMX30 enters Thursday in bull-market regime, +10.3% above 200-day MA with robust MACD and ADX 79.6 signaling sustained uptrend momentum. However, RSI-14 at 85.52 and Stochastic K/D both overbought (91.1/93.5) flag acute mean-reversion risk—index at upper Bollinger band (%B=0.97) leaves limited upside buffer. Continental Europe positive (CAC +71bp, DAX stable) and gold strength (+1.75%) support cyclicals and mining, but NASDAQ weakness (-0.83%) and elevated overbought readings warrant tactical caution. Dollar weakness (USD/SEK -44bp) provides mixed signals: headwind for Nordic exporters vs. modest currency tailwind for import-exposed sectors.
morningBrief: OMX30 bulls dominate technical setup with +10.3% above 200-MA and strong ADX trend, but extreme overbought conditions (RSI 85.5, Stochastic 91/93.5) demand discipline—watch for profit-taking into resistance near 3200 level (upper Bollinger). Support holds at 3085 (lower BB); yesterday's 3123 close is pivot. Industrials and Materials benefit from gold (+1.75%) and steady commodity backdrop, but USD/SEK weakness (-44bp) is headwind for Atlas Copco, Volvo, Ericsson—monitor closely. Banks likely NEUTRAL to POSITIVE despite 10Y yield dip (4.617%, -22bp) as structural NIM support remains. NASDAQ selloff (-83bp) adds sentiment risk to Tech/Telecom (Hexagon, Ericsson). Key watch: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—any surprise could spike VIX (at 15.88) and trigger overbought unwind. Bias remains BULLISH on trend but expect choppy consolidation with tactical pullbacks.
